text:
Dalibor Dvorsky is 21, fewer than 100 games into his NHL career, and starting to look like the scorer the Blues drafted 10th overall in 2023. He has five goals in 23 games while playing only about 12 minutes a night, and three of them came in his last ten, including a backhand against Anaheim on Nov. 17 that NHL.com called "Dvorsky backhands a beauty." He also had six points in six games for Slovakia at the Olympics in February.

The goals are mostly real. He has 3.59 expected goals (the quality of his chances), and his 14.7% shooting rate sits inside the range we'd expect for him. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking explains part of it: last season he got 1.8 shots per 60 off passes across the slot or from behind the net, the kind that go in about 25% of the time.

The rest of his game is still catching up. Evolving-Hockey had the Blues creating very little with him on the ice last season (bottom 1% of forwards), and this season they sit around even at five on five with him out there. Our range sees about 14 goals by season's end.
